sentences.text: 1 the said examination and was called for document verification.

Thereafter, a list of postings was issued by the department containing petitioner's name and his appointment letter was duly issued by Respondent No. 7.
2.3
On 24.12.2020, Director (Elementary Education) passed an order rejecting the candidature of the petitioner.

Thereafter, the petitioner approached the respondents and submitted various representations and on 03.08.2023, the respondents rejected his representations on the ground that a criminal case under Section 498A of IPC is pending against him.
Being aggrieved of the aforesaid, the present writ petition is filed.

3. The controversy in fact is not res integra as on an earlier occasion, I have had the opportunity to deal with a similarly situated candidate who was also embroiled in criminal proceedings arising out of his matrimonial discord.
4. The said decision was rendered in S.B. Civil Writ Petition No. 18747/2019 titled Patram Vs. State of Rajasthan & Ors.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
And the relevant thereof is extracted hereinbelow:-
"6.
Turning to the petitioner's case on its merits, it is acknowledged, as per the respondents' submitted response, that the petitioner did not withhold any information regarding the FIR against him.

Before joining his duties, he voluntarily disclosed the existence of FIR No.309/2019, registered at Police Station Anoopgarh,
District Sri Ganganagar, under Sections 498-A, 406, 323, 354 of IPC, initiated by his estranged wife due to marital discord.
Furthermore, the criminal trial stemming from this FIR has concluded with the petitioner's acquittal.

The only opposition at this stage for not allowing the petition is reliance placed by the learned counsel for the respondent on the Apex Court judgment rendered in Avtar Singh Vs. Union of India & Ors., reported in 2016 (8) SCC 471.
8.

entities.text: Avtar Singh Vs. Union of India & Ors., reported in 2016 (8) SCC 471
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having perused the judgment, ibid, what has to be borne in mind is that candidates must truthfully disclose information regarding convictions, acquittals,
arrests, or pending criminal cases to their employers, both before and after employment, without suppression or false statements.
Employers, when terminating services or canceling candidatures due to false information, should consider special circumstances and relevant government regulations.
Additionally, appropriate actions should be taken if there is suppression or false information regarding involvement in a criminal case, depending on its nature.
The accuracy and specificity of attestation/verification forms are crucial, and guilt for suppression or false suggestion requires attributable knowledge.

Employers, no doubt, can maintain their discretion in considering disclosed information and are not obligated to appoint Raj Kumar Solanki vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:7335) on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76807158/
2 candidates even if truthful disclosures are made, particularly in cases involving multiple pending cases or serious criminal offenses.

sentences.text: 9. In the instant case there is no allegation of suppression or concealment on the part of petitioner.
Even the offences, at the relevant time when he was embroiled in, did not in any manner impinge on the nature of duties which are/were to be performed by the petitioner.
Be that as it may, he in any case stands acquitted and has vindicated himself.
10. As an upshot of my discussion, as above, there is no justification for denying the petitioner appointment on the post he has been selected for."
5. As an upshot, I see no reason why the petitioner herein be also not given the benefit of the aforesaid view already expressed by me.

6. Consequently, the writ petition is allowed mandating the respondents to allow the petitioner to have the benefit of his performance in the selection process and offer him appointment in accordance with his merit subject of course, to the availability of vacancy available as on today.

In case, there is no vacancy available, the respondents are directed to consider the candidature of the petitioner on the basis of his performance in [2024:RJ-JD:7335] (4 of 4) [CW-13670/2023] the past selection process as and when the next first vacancy arises on the post in question.
7.. It is made clear that for the period petitioner has remained out of service, he shall not be entitled to any mandatory benefits on the principle of no work no pay.

8. In case the petitioner is offered appointment on the basis of availability of vacancy qua the advertisement in question, then he shall be entitled to notional benefits with seniority etc. along with his counterparts and were also allowed to join the services pursuant to the same selection process in which the petitioner had participated.
9. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
10. All pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

(ARUN MONGA),J 22-DhananjayS/-
